messages:
ops-bot: Incident alert: spike in 429s from /v1/generate across region us-east-1 for customer tenant=acme-corp. 1min error rate 18% (baseline 0.3%).

Maria (Support): seeing multiple customer tickets about timeouts + 429. They report low token usage in their app — definitely looks like a server-side limiter problem. Escalating to eng-sre.

Devon (Eng-SRE): on it. grabbing logs for tenant=acme-corp and global limiter metrics. any config deploys in last hour?

Chloe (Eng-Infra): I rolled out a limiter config change to the shared-token-bucket yesterday 02:12 UTC to tighten burst window (we reduced burst_capacity from 200 to 20 for cost reasons). It was staged to 10% canary, then promoted at 04:30 UTC.

Samir (Eng-Runtime): that sounds suspect — some long-tail customers rely on larger bursts. What exactly changed?

Chloe (Eng-Infra): config snippet: ```yaml
rate_limiter:
  type: token_bucket
  refill_rate_per_sec: 50
  burst_capacity: 20    # was 200
  per_tenant: true
```

Devon (Eng-SRE): logs show a flood of 429s with header X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0 for many tokens even though their per-minute usage is < 10 requests/min. Looks like burst_capacity cut the initial allowance so short-lived traffic hits limit.

Maria (Support): customer says they had a scheduled batch that kicked off and got hammered by 429s — their code retries and it amplified latency. They're asking for timeline + rollback.

jlee (SRE Lead): rollback to previous limiter config (burst_capacity 200) across hosts in us-east-1 immediately. Do a gradual rollout with health checks.

Chloe (Eng-Infra): starting rollback now. Will push old config to canary first and watch metrics.

Devon (Eng-SRE): while Chloe rolls back, we should apply a short-term mitigation: whitelist tenant=acme-corp and a small set of high-risk tenants from the tightened config so they stop hitting the bucket. Can we hotpatch that?

Chloe (Eng-Infra): yes we can add tenant whitelist in the rate-limiter policy store. Pushing change: ```sh
POST /infra/config/rate-limit/whitelist
{ "tenants": ["acme-corp", "delta-ml"] }
```

ops-bot: Deploy started: rollback limiter-config v2 -> v1. Canary hosts (12) updated. Monitoring: 429-rate and latency.

Devon (Eng-SRE): noticed that the limiter service was mis-reading X-Forwarded-For headers for a subset of requests, grouping different clients under same bucket key. That made the effective consumption look higher. Adding that to root-cause.

Samir (Eng-Runtime): reproduction steps for the bug: 1) send rapid identical requests from multiple source IPs with same API-key header; 2) limiter code truncates key to first 8 chars for some cache keys; 3) bucket counter aggregated by truncated key. Example curl: ```bash
for i in {1..50}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOP" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"input":"hello"}' &
done
```

Devon (Eng-SRE): confirmed. Found PR that changed key hashing last month (PR#4582). It introduced a fallback that uses truncated token when hashing fails. Hash failures spiked after we rotated HMAC salts during maintenance.

Chloe (Eng-Infra): rollback complete to v1 across canary, promoting to all hosts now. 429-rate dropping in canary. Will finish full rollout in ~5min.

ops-bot: Rollout complete: limiter-config v1 on 120 hosts. Global 429s for /v1/generate back to baseline 0.4% in 3m.

Maria (Support): told customer we've rolled back config, added a tenant whitelist, and are doing a post-incident review. They asked for ETA on permanent fix.

jlee (SRE Lead): action items: 1) Samir to revert fallback-to-truncated-hash in limiter and add robust error handling for hash failures (owner: Samir, due: 2026-03-18). 2) Chloe to add canary health gating for limiter changes (automated check: 429 <= baseline+1% in 10m) (owner: Chloe, due: 2026-03-17). 3) Devon to produce brief postmortem and customer-facing timeline (owner: Devon, due: 2026-03-16). 4) Maria to follow up with acme-corp and offer credit for downtime (owner: Maria, due: 2026-03-15).

Samir (Eng-Runtime): patch prepared. Will open PR and request expedited review. Also adding unit test that simulates HMAC salt rotation.

Devon (Eng-SRE): logging improvements: emit limiter-key-derived and hash_ok boolean in access logs for easier debugging. Will send patch.

Chloe (Eng-Infra): postmortem note: we promoted a config that reduced burst_capacity without tenant impact analysis. Need a pre-promotion checklist for per-tenant risk. Will add to runbook.

Maria (Support): customer update sent: apologised, explained rollback + whitelist + timeline for permanent fix. They appreciated the quick response but asked for SLA credit.

jlee (SRE Lead): good triage. After PRs merge, schedule a tabletop walk-through of the incident with product + support to ensure communication is clear.

Devon (Eng-SRE): creating incident doc now and attaching logs, diffs, and the sequence of actions. Will link when ready.

Maria (Support): thanks team. closing channel on customer comms for now. If anything else flares, ping here. :thumbsup:
